A bicycle is a human-powered vehicle that allows for efficient and eco-friendly transportation. It consists of several key components that work together to enable movement. At the core of the bicycle is the frame, which provides structural support and connects all the parts. The frame is typically made of steel, aluminum, or carbon fiber, and it includes the front and rear wheels, handlebars, and a seat.

The wheels are attached to the frame via axles and bearings, allowing them to rotate smoothly. The front wheel is usually steered by the handlebars, which are connected to the fork, enabling the rider to change direction. The rear wheel is connected to the drivetrain, which includes the pedals, chain, and gears. When the rider pedals, the motion is transferred through the chain to the rear gear, which turns the rear wheel, propelling the bicycle forward.

The gears allow the rider to adjust the resistance based on the terrain, making it easier to climb hills or maintain speed on flat surfaces. The brakes, typically located on the handlebars, provide a way to slow down or stop the bicycle by applying pressure to the wheels via brake pads.
